_note: Per iOS screen (SweepFrames.swift names): its Android status (not-ported, in-progress, parity) and the differences still open. Read by scripts/android_parity.py. DECISIONS.md 2026-11-10.

_android_forced.why: Android's system back gesture and button close the top sheet or page, as every Android app does.

Airbnb's line (Hidde, 2026-11-10: "Yes, Airbnb's line"): brand, type, colour, layout and our own icons are the iPhone's; the system signs take Android's form, drawn in the same set (Material Symbols Rounded) at the iPhone's weight: back is the arrow (←) where the iPhone draws chevron.left, share is Android's three connected dots where it draws square.and.arrow.up, and the overflow menu is the vertical dots (⋮) where it draws ellipsis.circle. Source: CONVENTIONS.md, "One app on iPhone and Android" (2026-11-10).
The location and camera questions are the system's own dialogs.

Continue with Apple and Continue with Google open in a Custom Tab, Supabase's ordinary OAuth redirect, the website's route; the iPhone shows Apple's own sheet for Apple and ASWebAuthenticationSession for Google. Same pills, words, order and account.
Android's own bars at the top and bottom of the screen.

SF Pro, the iPhone's system face, exists only on Apple platforms; Android sets every text in Inter (OFL), the open face closest to it, at the same sizes and weights and tracked as SF tracks per size (ui/Text.kt). The brand face Gabarito is the same on both. Icons are no longer a difference: Material Symbols Rounded, the closest open set to SF Symbols, generated glyph for glyph (DECISIONS.md 2026-11-10).
The share circle on a tree's card opens Android's share sheet with the same tagged link (utm_campaign=map_card).
The Species chip's list is a system sheet on both phones: SwiftUI's .sheet on the iPhone, Material's modal bottom sheet on Android.

The iPhone asks once between Apple Maps and Google Maps and remembers it; Android has no Apple Maps, so its place in the same question is Another maps app, which hands the spot to Android's own chooser (a geo: link that Waze, OsmAnd and every maps app answer). Google Maps opens the same walking-route link as on the iPhone.
The report menu on a tree page is the system's own pop-up menu on both phones: SwiftUI's Menu on the iPhone, Material's dropdown menu on Android.

A modal sheet is Material's bottom sheet on Android and SwiftUI's .sheet on the iPhone. The fitted one is drawn as the iPhone draws it on iOS 26: laid out at the screen's full width and scaled to stand 8 in from each side and 10 above the bottom, so its words wrap where the iPhone's do (measured 2026-11-11: the review-ask tile 53 for its 56, the sign-in title 258 for the 271 Core Text sets). Content, sizes and order are the same.

Android's photo picker removes a photograph's location before the app sees it, so a photograph chosen from the library always asks where the tree stands (the iPhone reads it off the photograph). The camera path is the same on both.
The iPhone keeps a copy on the phone and sends it in the background; Android keeps nothing on the phone (hard rule 11), so it sends at once and says so when it did not arrive.
Open Settings lands on the app's own page in Android's Settings, and the recovery sheet's path line names Android's path; Rate the app opens the Play Store.
The iPhone's Yes opens Apple's rating dialog; Android's opens Google Play's own review card (the Play review library), the platform's equivalent.

_android_forced.what: Glyphs the open set does not have
_android_forced.why: Every icon comes from Material Symbols Rounded (android/generate_symbols.py), never traced from SF Symbols. Where the set has no glyph of the SF shape, the nearest one stands in (visual review 2026-11-11): map.fill is the set's map, whose middle panel is drawn open; leaf is the set's eco leaf, flipped so it lies as the iPhone's does; arrow.turn.up.right is the set's reply arrow, flipped; sparkles and the early adopter's sparkle are auto_awesome (one four-point star has no glyph of its own), from Google's repository of the same set; building.2 is domain; mappin, a ball on a needle, is keep, the set's pin on a needle; person.badge.plus is person_add, whose plus has no disc; ruler is straighten; bubble.left is chat_bubble; ticket is confirmation_number. Sizes and weights are the iPhone's: SF points x 4/3 in dp, weight 600 for semibold, 700 for bold.

differences: First launch reads the 11.5 MB catalogue in about ten seconds on the one-core emulator under a loaded Mac; later launches read a binary snapshot. Not yet measured on a real phone.

closed.glass: The iPhone's frosted material behind the tab bar, its camera disc and the round buttons over the tree's photograph: a backdrop blur on Android 12+ through Haze 1.7.2 (RenderEffect, API 31; developer.android.com/reference/android/graphics/RenderEffect), opaque ground below 31.
